sourceIssues.locator: Published version, Publ. Math. IHÉS 128 (2018), 121–218 (Numdam PDF, SHA-256 e2b4a076…); Lemma 3.1.9 and its proof, printed p. 166
sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 3.1.9. — Let a_R = m²_R + pR. There is a canonical commutative diagram [M̃₁ ⊗_{Ŵ(R)} Ŵ(R/a_R) → φ*(M_{R/a_R}); D̃₁ ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R) → φ*(D) ⊗_W Ŵ(R/a_R)] where the horizontal maps are induced by the natural inclusions M̃₁ → φ*(M_R) and D̃₁ → φ*(D). Proof. — L ⊕ T be a normal decomposition for (M_{R/a_R}, M_{R/a_R,1}), and let L₀ ⊕ T₀ be the induced normal decomposition for (D, D₁).
sourceIssues.correction: The construction has to be replaced by the one of KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15, which follows [Ho23] and, in essence, Zink's [Zi99, Theorem 3].
sourceIssues.reason: The map produced by the printed proof depends on the chosen normal decomposition M = L ⊕ T, so it is not canonical and the diagram does not characterise it: as KPZ26 Remark 5.1.17(a) puts it, « the isomorphism which is given by the construction of [KP18, Lem. 3.1.9] is not canonical and hence not “correct” », and the diagram does not determine c because its horizontal maps are not always injective, which can happen even when cW(R) is p-torsion free. Consequently [KP18, Lem. 3.1.12] does not hold with c defined as in the proof of Lemma 3.1.9.
sourceIssues.known: Known and corrected by the authors themselves: KPZ26 §1.3.1 and Remark 5.1.17(a)–(b); the replacement is KPZ26 Lemma 5.1.15. Pointed out by M. Hoff, [Ho23, Rem. 2.29].

sourceIssues.printed: 3.2.12. — … Choose an isomorphism Ψ_{R_G} : M̃_{R_G,1} ≅ M_{R_G} which respects the s_{α,0}, and such that Ψ_{R_G} is constant modulo a_{R_E} … Note that this is possible as G is smooth, and if Ψ_{R_G} is constant modulo a_{R_E} then the map M̃_{R_G,1} ⊗_{Ŵ(R_G)} Ŵ(R_G/a_{R_E}) → M_{R_G/a_{R_E}} does respect the s_{α,0}.
sourceIssues.correction: An isomorphism Ψ_{R_G} as described exists only under the additional hypothesis that the Hodge embedding is **very good** in the sense of KPZ26 Definition 5.2.5. Smoothness of G alone does not give it. Lemma 3.2.14 and Propositions 3.2.17 and 3.3.13 are then valid with the same proofs, under that hypothesis.
sourceIssues.reason: This is the omitted condition behind the gap the sequel describes as serious: the condition « is needed for the construction in [KP18, §3] of the universal deformation of a p-divisible group equipped with crystalline tensors ». The printed justification — that Ψ_{R_G} exists because G is smooth — does not establish that the canonical transport of the corrected Lemma 3.1.9 preserves the tensors.

sourceIssues.printed: Theorem 4.2.7. — Under the above assumptions, there exists a diagram of morphisms (4.2.8) S̃_K(G,X)_{O_E} → S_K(G,X)_{O_E}, S̃_K(G,X)_{O_E} → M^loc_{G,X} … Theorem 4.6.23. — If G₂ splits over a tamely ramified extension of Q_p, then there exists a Shimura datum of Hodge type (G,X) such that the conditions of Corollary 4.6.15 are satisfied … (1) S_{K°_{2,p}}(G₂,X₂) is étale locally isomorphic to M^loc_{G,X}.
sourceIssues.correction: Theorem 4.2.7 and Corollaries 4.2.12 and 4.2.13 require the additional hypothesis that the Hodge embedding is very good; Theorem 4.2.7 should be replaced by KPZ26 Theorem 7.1.3, and the final Theorem 4.6.23 by KPZ26 Theorem 7.2.21. The remaining arguments of §4 are unaffected and their conclusions hold once the Hodge embeddings appearing in them are assumed very good.
sourceIssues.reason: These statements consume §§3.1–3.3 through Ψ_{R_G}, so they inherit the omitted condition of E2. The sequel is explicit that this is the propagation of a « serious gap in [KP18] », which also reached earlier versions of [KZ25].
sourceIssues.known: Known and corrected by the authors themselves: KPZ26 §1.3.1, which says that [KP18, Theorem 4.2.7] and [KP18, Cor. 4.2.12, Cor. 4.2.13] « now require the additional assumption that the Hodge embedding is very good », that 4.2.7 « should be replaced by Theorem 7.1.3 » and that this « affects the final statement [KP18, Theorem 4.6.23] … which should be replaced by Theorem 7.2.21 ». KPZ26 §1.3.2 also notes that its own Theorem 1.1.2 is slightly weaker than [KP18, Thm. 4.6.23] for factors of exceptional type A, a restriction removed by its Corollary 1.1.3.

sourceIssues.printed: q_loc : M̃^loc_G → M^loc_{G,X} by taking (f,F) to f⁻¹(F). One sees easily that q_loc is a G-torsor. Thus we have a diagram (4.2.9) M̃^loc_G → M^loc_G, M̃^loc_G → M^loc_{G,X}, with π_loc and q_loc are G-torsors.
sourceIssues.correction: q_loc is not a G-torsor. It is isomorphic to the action morphism G × M^loc_{G,X} → M^loc_{G,X}, which is smooth because it is the composition of the isomorphism (g,m) ↦ (g, g·m) of G × M^loc_{G,X} with the projection to M^loc_{G,X}; the rest of the proof is unchanged.
sourceIssues.reason: Smoothness of q, not the torsor property, is what the theorem needs; the printed assertion is simply false for q_loc, while π_loc is a G-torsor.

sourceIssues.printed: Hence, it suffices to give a complete separated topology τ on Ŵ(A) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p such that for any x ∈ W(m_A), p^{−m}φ^m(x) → 0. Indeed, then the sum s̃ = s + Σ_{m≥0} Φ^{m+1} ∘ s ∘ Φ₀^{−m−1} − Φ^m ∘ s ∘ Φ₀^{−m} converges to an element of Hom_W(D,M) ⊗ Q_p in τ and is Frobenius invariant.
sourceIssues.correction: The ring cW(A)[1/p] is not complete for the topology τ defined there, so establishing p^{−m}φ^m(x) → 0 in τ does not finish the proof. KPZ26 show instead that cW(A)[1/p] is p-adically complete and separated and that p^{−m}φ^m(x) → 0 in the p-adic topology for x ∈ cW(M_A), which does finish it, using Zink's logarithmic coordinates on cW(pN) and [Zi01, Prop. 2.3, 2.4].
sourceIssues.reason: The convergence argument needs completeness of the ring in the topology in which the series is summed; the printed topology τ does not have it.
sourceIssues.known: Known and corrected by the authors themselves: KPZ26 §7.3.1(2), « Correction to the proof of [KP18, Lem. 3.1.17] », which thanks M. Hoff for pointing this out.

sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 4.6.13. — There is an isomorphism of Ē-schemes with G₂(A^p_f) × Gal(Ē/E′)-action Sh_{K°_{2,p}}(G₂,X₂) ≅ [[Sh_{K°_p}(G,X)⁺ × A(G_{2,Z_{(p)}})]/A(G_{Z_{(p)}})°]^{|J|}.
sourceIssues.correction: The connected Shimura varieties in the disjoint union must carry different levels, conjugated by the elements j ∈ J of §4.6.12: writing Sh_{K°_p}(G,X)^{j,+} for the connected component containing (j,X⁺), which is isomorphic to Sh_{jK°_p j^{−1}}(G,X)⁺, the correct description is Sh_{K°_{2,p}}(G₂,X₂) ≅ ⨆_{j∈J} [Sh_{K°_p}(G,X)^{j,+} × A(G_{2,Z_{(p)}})]/A(G_{Z_{(p)}})°, and correspondingly the integral model of Corollary 4.6.15 is ⨆_{j∈J} [S_{K°_p}(G,X)^{j,+} × A(G_{2,Z_{(p)}})]/A(G_{Z_{(p)}})°, with S_{K°_p}(G,X)^{j,+} the Zariski closure of Sh_{K°_p}(G,X)^{j,+}.
sourceIssues.reason: As printed the union is the |J|-fold power of one space at the single level K°_p, which is not what the quotient by K°_{2,p} produces; the stabiliser computation Stab(jA(G_{2,Z_{(p)}})) = jK°_p j^{−1} ∩ Ã(G_{Z_{(p)}})° is what forces the conjugated levels. The same proof as Corollary 4.6.15 then works, the corrected scheme having the right generic fibre.

sourceIssues.printed: 4.6.21. — Let (H,Y) be a Shimura datum with H^ad a classical group. Recall ([20], cf. [43] 3.4.13) that there is central isogeny H̃ → H♯ (which depends also on Y if H has a factor of type D) such that (H,Y) is of abelian type if and only if H^der is a quotient of H♯.
sourceIssues.correction: H♯ is not defined for every (H,Y) with H of classical type; the construction needs a further condition on (H,Y), which is satisfied when (H^ad,Y^ad) is of abelian type.
sourceIssues.reason: The assertion is stated for all classical (H,Y) but the cited construction does not apply that generally.
sourceIssues.known: Known and corrected by the authors themselves: KPZ26 p. 80, footnote 8: « In [KP18, 4.6.21] it is incorrectly asserted that H♯ is defined for any (H,Y) with H of classical type, however H may not satisfy the third condition above. This is however satisfied if (H^ad,Y^ad) is of abelian type. »

sourceIssues.printed: The corresponding local model M^loc_{GL(V′),{μ₀},y} over Z_p is the smooth Grassmannian Gr(V′_{Z_p}) classifying subbundles F ⊂ V′_{Z_p} ⊗_{Z_p} O_S of rank dim_{Q_p}(V′).
sourceIssues.correction: … of rank (1/2)·dim_{Q_p}(V′), the rank of the Hodge filtration of the symplectic Hodge embedding into GSp(V′, ψ′).
sourceIssues.reason: μ₀ is the minuscule cocharacter of GL(V′) coming from a Hodge embedding into GSp(V′, ψ′), whose Hodge filtration is Lagrangian, of rank half the dimension. Subbundles of rank dim V′ would be the whole bundle, and the Grassmannian of them a point. The extraction recorded the correction in its item M13 (Gr(g′, Λ′) with 2g′ = dim V′).
